hook: The Sun King, who built Versailles and reigned for 72 years.

pages.x: Louis was born in 1638, a "gift from God" to parents who had been childless for 23 years. He became king at four. During a revolt of nobles, a mob broke into the palace at night to check the boy king was still there; he pretended to be asleep. He never forgot it.

When his chief minister died in 1661, Louis, 22, announced he would rule alone. He took the sun as his emblem and danced the part of Apollo, the sun god, in court ballets. "I am the state," he is supposed to have said.

He turned his father's hunting lodge at Versailles into the grandest palace in Europe, with the Hall of Mirrors and gardens with some 1,400 fountains. Thousands of nobles lived there, competing to hand him his shirt in the morning, and were too busy to rebel.
He paid for the Academy of Sciences, the Paris Observatory, the plays of Molière and the music of Lully. French became the language of royal courts and diplomats all over Europe.
For decades he fought his neighbours for land and glory, and France became the strongest power in Europe. But the wars, above all the War of the Spanish Succession, left France deep in debt.
In 1685 he cancelled the edict that protected France's Protestants. Some 200,000 Huguenots fled to England, the Netherlands, Prussia and America, taking their skills with them.

He reigned for 72 years, longer than any other monarch in European history, outliving his son and grandson. Dying, he told his five-year-old great-grandson, the next king: "I have loved war too much; do not copy me in that."
Louis XIV made France the leading power and the cultural model of Europe, and kings everywhere copied Versailles. But his wars and spending left debts that helped bring on the French Revolution.
pts: Reigned 72 years, the longest in European history
Made France the leading power in Europe
